extracted.intended_audience: readers interested in research integrity, science policy, and retractions (scientists, journalists, policy watchers)
extracted.subtask_description: A news report describing a scientist's resignation from a government science post after criticism for co-authoring a fraudulent stem cell paper, including reactions about qualifications, integrity, and policy implications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Qualification for science leadership
rubrics_metrics.description: Assess whether an appointee is qualified, innovative, and prepared to conduct the job of overseeing national R&D.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Critics argued Park 'never proved she is innovative and prepared to conduct that job.' One critic said: 'First of all, she is a typical scientist who follows political power merely for one’s ambition not for people’s benefit.' The article highlights concerns that a person in this position should be capable of conducting an 'innovative R&D plan' for the country.

rubrics_metrics.name: Authorship diligence and responsibility
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors should exercise care before accepting co-authorship and ensure the integrity of the work they are attaching their name to.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Park apologized: 'I think I was not careful enough to be a co-author of Hwang Woo-suk’s paper that was published in Science…I am deeply regretful.' The reporting frames co-authorship of fabricated research as a substantive failure of due diligence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Past research integrity as a factor in suitability
rubrics_metrics.description: Past involvement in fraudulent or retracted research is a relevant consideration when evaluating someone's suitability for high-level science positions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The article emphasizes Park's co-authorship of one of the stem cell papers by Woo-Suk Hwang, which 'had been fabricated' and led to resignation from an earlier advisory role; it also references Hwang's later conviction for embezzling research funds. These facts are presented as the basis for public criticism and as grounds for questioning suitability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Currency and relevance of proposed innovation strategy
rubrics_metrics.description: Leaders should promote up-to-date innovation strategies rather than decade-old approaches.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A critic said Park 'is promoting an innovation strategy that is now a decade old' and warned 'This approach will bring tragedy to Korean R&D, not innovation.' The reporting uses this to argue that proposed policy direction and its timeliness matter when evaluating an appointee.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accountability and transparency in appointments
rubrics_metrics.description: The degree of oversight required for appointments (e.g., parliamentary approval) and the visibility of decision-making affect public acceptance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The article notes Park’s position 'would have given her a say over the country’s R&D budget... The appointment does not require approval from parliament,' and frames lack of such checks as a source of criticism and public concern.
